summary: Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive, cinematic web experience that tells the stories of the machines, instruments, and hardware humanity left behind on the Moon and Mars. Rather than treating abandoned equipment as debris, the project presents each piece as a story with its own history, purpose, and reason for being left. This addresses the challenge by making space history tangible to a general audience and by showing how exploration plans change over time. Some of this equipment outlived the programs that built it, and some hardware was kept for later missions. The project is meant to show that what we leave behind is part of the record of how we explore.
details:
What the project does

Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an immersive digital field study and interactive web platform that catalogs and honors the machines, instruments, and hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. Traversing six lunar landing regions and four Martian provinces, the platform features:

  • Cinematic Narrative Journey: An atmospheric, scroll-driven experience guiding visitors from Earth orbit to the Apollo landing sites, through interplanetary transit, and across the Martian surface.
  • Comprehensive Artifact Catalog: Deep-dive dossier cards for 14 iconic artifacts—including the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles (LRV), the nuclear-powered ALSEP experiment network, Lunar Module descent stages, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Spirit, InSight, and the Ingenuity helicopter.
  • Real-Time 3D WebGL Surface Exploration: Interactive Three.js/React Three Fiber 3D environments allowing users to inspect procedurally reconstructed hardware and terrain in real time.
  • Synthesized Space Soundscapes: A custom procedural audio engine built on the Web Audio API that translates the contrast between the airless acoustic vacuum of the Moon (suit breathing, radio static, telemetry hum) and the low-pressure winds of Mars.

Benefits

  • Shifts the Paradigm on Space Heritage: Replaces the perception of discarded space hardware as "debris" with an understanding of these sites as historical, archaeological landmarks of human achievement.
  • Bridges Science and Emotion: Contextualizes dry engineering data—such as sol counts, battery lifespans, and traverses—within human stories of perseverance, unexpected discoveries (e.g., Spirit’s broken wheel uncovering silica hot springs), and poignant mission conclusions.
  • Zero-Barrier Educational Tool: Requires no specialized software, app installation, or user account. It functions on any modern web browser across mobile, tablet, and desktop devices.

Intended impact

Our goal is to inspire students, educators, and space enthusiasts by making space history visceral, tangible, and personal. As NASA’s Artemis campaign prepares to return humans to the Moon and lay the groundwork for crewed Mars missions, understanding what earlier explorers left behind fosters an ethical awareness of planetary preservation and cultural heritage. The project serves as an open educational resource that demonstrates how open NASA data can be synthesized into modern web experiences.

Tools and languages used

  • Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript (ESNext), HTML5, CSS3.
  • Frontend Framework & Build System: React 19, Vite, PostCSS, Tailwind CSS.
  • 3D Graphics & Animation: Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), GSAP (GreenSock) & ScrollTrigger, Framer Motion, Lenis kinetic smooth scrolling.
  • Audio & Signal Processing: Web Audio API, procedural mathematical sound synthesis (custom DSP node script generating looped telemetry, oscillators, and filtered noise).
  • Asset Processing & Performance: Sharp image pipeline for next-generation WebP responsive image generation, Fontsource typography (Instrument Serif, Manrope).
  • Hosting & CI/CD: Vercel edge deployment with automated preview pipelines.

How it's creative

  • Atmospheric Storytelling: Unlike standard tabular databases or static galleries, the project employs kinetic typography, scroll-linked camera sweeps, and lighting cues that emulate authentic lunar contrasts and Martian atmospheric scattering.
  • Zero-Sample Procedural Audio: Rather than relying on generic, copyrighted stock music, all ambient soundscapes are procedurally generated from raw mathematical waveforms, filtered white noise, and oscillators to capture the physical reality of space vacuum and planetary telemetry.
  • Dual Perspective Exploration: Users can switch between orbital field studies and on-the-ground historical reconstructions to understand both the macro geographical layout and the micro engineering components of each artifact.

Factors considered

  • Historical & Scientific Accuracy: All coordinates, mission dates, sol counts, and landing site topologies were verified against official NASA mission reports, JPL logs, and the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal.
  • Universal Accessibility & Progressive Enhancement: Engineered with a complete semantic HTML and inline styling fallback within the page's initial DOM. If a user has low bandwidth, network latency, or disabled JavaScript, the full story, stats, and artifact dossiers render immediately. It also respects the prefers-reduced-motion operating system setting.
  • Mobile Responsiveness & Performance: Optimized lightweight WebP assets, aggressive asset preloading, and dynamic WebGL canvas scaling ensure 60fps performance across smartphones and laptops alike.
